title: Compactness of a constructible sheaf against uniformly bounded families
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, in the standing setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Fix an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=\underline E$ or $\underline{\Qlb}$ be the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], and let $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All sheaves below are $\Lambda_X$-module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and all Hom groups and direct sums are in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)=D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. In particular no derived-completion condition is imposed.

Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of constructible sheaves [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for the full subcategory of filtered colimits of constructible sheaves computed in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$, and
$$
\Dic(X,\Lambda)=\{K\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X}):H^n(K)\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)\text{ for all }n\in\mathbf Z\}.
$$
Let $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$, viewed as a complex concentrated in degree $0$, let $a\le b$ be integers, let $I$ be a small set in the fixed universe, and let $(K_\lambda)_{\lambda\in I}$ be a family in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ with $H^n(K_\lambda)=0$ for $n\notin[a,b]$ and every $\lambda$. Then for every $s\in\mathbf Z$ the natural homomorphism
$$
\alpha_s:\bigoplus_{\lambda\in I}\Hom(C,K_\lambda[s])\longrightarrow\Hom\bigl(C,(\bigoplus_{\lambda\in I}K_\lambda)[s]\bigr),\qquad (f_\lambda)\longmapsto\sum_\lambda\iota_\lambda[s]\circ f_\lambda,
$$
is an isomorphism. The sum in this formula is finite because $(f_\lambda)$ has finite support, and $\iota_\lambda$ denotes the coprojection. The shift convention is $(K[s])^n=K^{n+s}$.

proof.text: For $N\in\mathbf N$, let $P(N)$ mean the asserted bijectivity for every pair $a\le b$ with $b-a=N$, every family with that common bound, and every shift $s\in\mathbf Z$. Induct on $N$, keeping all shifts in the inductive assertion. Empty families give the map between zero groups, and are also included in this induction.

source.place: Proof, opening sentence: induction on b-a for all s simultaneously

proof.text: Suppose $a=b$. Set $B_\lambda=H^a(K_\lambda)$; this is in $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ by the definition of $\Dic$. For a representing complex, the inclusion $\tau_{\le a}K_\lambda\to K_\lambda$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees $\le a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], and both sides have zero cohomology above $a$. The projection $j_a:\tau_{\le a}K_\lambda\to B_\lambda[-a]$ in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] induces $\ker d^a/\operatorname{im}d^{a-1}\to B_\lambda$ identically in degree $a$; its other cohomology maps are between zero objects. These are quasi-isomorphisms and hence invertible in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Thus $K_\lambda\simeq B_\lambda[-a]$.

source.place: Proof, base case a=b: K_lambda is B_lambda[-a]

proof.text:
By [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1), coproducts are computed termwise on complexes. Consequently the coproduct of the $B_\lambda[-a]$ is $(\bigoplus_\lambda B_\lambda)[-a]$, and shifting this coproduct by $s$ agrees with the coproduct of the shifts: both have exactly the same terms and signed differentials. Under the isomorphisms in step 2, $\alpha_s$ is precisely
$$\bigoplus_\lambda\Ext^{s-a}(C,B_\lambda)\longrightarrow\Ext^{s-a}(C,\bigoplus_\lambda B_\lambda),$$
where, for every integer $q$, $\Ext^q(C,B)$ denotes $\Hom_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})}(C[0],B[0][q])$. This map is an isomorphism by [det-ind-heart-ii-sums], whose statement allows every integer $q$, with $q=s-a$. The identification respects the natural map since a summand $f$ is sent to the shifted coprojection composed with $f$. This proves $P(0)$.

source.place: Proof, base case: identify the comparison with Ext^{s-a} and apply sk-cor-ind-heart-ii

proof.text:
Now take $b>a$ and suppose $P(N)$ holds for $N<b-a$. Put $A_\lambda=\tau_{\le b-1}K_\lambda$ and $B_\lambda=H^b(K_\lambda)[-b]$. The cohomology formula in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology] shows that $A_\lambda$ has cohomology in $[a,b-1]$; the definition of a one-term complex shows that $B_\lambda$ has cohomology in $[b,b]$, with its single sheaf ind-constructible. Moreover $A_\lambda\in\Dic$ by [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] with $q=b$ and identify $\tau_{\le b}K_\lambda\simeq K_\lambda$, since its inclusion is a quasi-isomorphism by the same cohomology formula [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. We obtain distinguished triangles
$$T_\lambda:\quad A_\lambda\xrightarrow{u_\lambda}K_\lambda\xrightarrow{v_\lambda}B_\lambda\xrightarrow{\delta_\lambda}A_\lambda[1].$$

source.place: Proof, induction step: truncation triangles and the two smaller cohomological intervals

proof.text: The componentwise coproduct of the $T_\lambda$ is a distinguished triangle by [det-def-localizing-closure-existence](1), with objects $A=\bigoplus A_\lambda$, $K=\bigoplus K_\lambda$, $B=\bigoplus B_\lambda$, and boundary $\delta:B\to A[1]$ induced by the $\delta_\lambda$. The shift/coproduct identification is the termwise one from step 3. Each coprojection triple is a morphism of these triangles: for example $\delta\,\iota^B_\lambda=\iota^A_\lambda[1]\,\delta_\lambda$, by the definition of the coproduct arrow. By [det-ambient-ind-derived-sums](1), the sum objects are in $\Dic$ and retain the respective bounds $[a,b-1]$, $[a,b]$, $[b,b]$. The argument only needs this sum triangle, not an additional theorem identifying it with a chosen truncation triangle of $K$.

source.place: Proof, induction step: a direct sum of distinguished triangles is distinguished; cohomology commutes with direct sums

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to each $T_\lambda$, to its rotations and to the sum triangle. The rotations and shifts are those of [def-weil-triangulated-category]; repeated rotation supplies the exact Hom sequence in every integer degree, with the usual signed connecting maps. Thus, for fixed $s$, obtain a commutative diagram whose top row is the direct sum of the five-term exact sequences
$$\Hom(C,B_\lambda[s-1])\longrightarrow\Hom(C,A_\lambda[s])\longrightarrow\Hom(C,K_\lambda[s])\longrightarrow\Hom(C,B_\lambda[s])\longrightarrow\Hom(C,A_\lambda[s+1]),$$
and whose bottom row is the analogous sequence for $(A,K,B)$. The top row is exact: a finitely supported tuple in a kernel has a preimage in each of its finitely many nonzero components, and these preimages form a finitely supported tuple; the reverse inclusion follows from zero composites. The vertical maps are the comparison maps $\alpha$ for these families. They commute with every arrow, including the connecting arrows: for $h:C\to B_\lambda[s-1]$ the boundary identity from step 5 gives $\delta[s-1]\iota^B_\lambda[s-1]h=\iota^A_\lambda[s]\delta_\lambda[s-1]h$; summing these identities proves the connecting square, and the squares for $u,v$ follow by the identical coprojection equation. Here the Hom-exactness lemma supplies exactness, rather than a definition of a homological functor being used as a theorem.

source.place: Proof, induction step: the natural ladder of five-term Hom sequences

proof.text: The vertical maps in positions $1,2,4,5$ of the diagram in step 6 are bijective: use $P(0)$ for the $B_\lambda$ family at shifts $s-1,s$, and $P(b-a-1)$ for the $A_\lambda$ family at shifts $s,s+1$. For completeness write either exact row as $L\xrightarrow{d_1}M\xrightarrow{d_2}N\xrightarrow{d_3}P\xrightarrow{d_4}Q$ and the vertical maps as $f_L,\ldots,f_Q$, with primes for the bottom row. If $f_N(n)=0$, then $f_Pd_3(n)=0$, so $d_3(n)=0$ and $n=d_2(m)$. Since $d'_2f_M(m)=0$, write $f_M(m)=d'_1(l')$; lift $l'$ along $f_L$ to $l$. Injectivity of $f_M$ gives $m=d_1(l)$ and hence $n=0$. For $n'\in N'$, lift $d'_3(n')$ along $f_P$ to $p$. Since $f_Qd_4(p)=d'_4d'_3(n')=0$, injectivity of $f_Q$ gives $p=d_3(n)$ for some $n$. Then $n'-f_N(n)=d'_2(m')$; lift $m'$ along $f_M$ and add its image under $d_2$ to $n$. This gives a preimage of $n'$. Thus $f_N=\alpha_s$ is bijective. This proves $P(b-a)$ for every $s$ and finishes the induction.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: the four outer vertical maps are isomorphisms, so the middle one is (five-lemma diagram chase)

proof_origin.place: Full proof in sk-thm-constructible-compactness-bounded.proof.md, with explicit cohomology checks, naturality and diagram chase
